skill.name: matplotlib
skill.description: Create Matplotlib plots, publication figures, and style configurations with Python plotting guidance and local helper scripts.
skill.summary: Guides Python users through Matplotlib plotting, styling, export, and troubleshooting workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, Matplotlib plotting terminology, and official documentation links. One medium filesystem issue remains because scripts/style_configurator.py writes to a caller-supplied output path without restriction. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious network behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict --output to a project-local directory, require a .mplstyle extension, and refuse parent directory or absolute paths.

remediation.issue: Helper script execution expectations are implicit
remediation.suggestion: State that helper scripts should run only after user confirmation and with user-selected output paths.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **Always use the OO interface** - Avoid pyplot state machine
| Distributions comparison | Box plot, Violin plot | Overlaid histograms |
# Grid behind or in front of data
alpha = input("  Grid transparency (0-1, default 0.3): ").strip() or '0.3'
For comprehensive plot type examples and variations, refer to `references/plot_types.md`.
For detailed styling options and colormap guidelines, see `references/styling_guide.md`.
- `dpi`: Resolution (300 for publications, 150 for web, 72 for screen)
- `facecolor='white'`: Ensures white background (useful for transparent themes)
- Set figsize at creation: `fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))`
- Use `constrained_layout=True` or `tight_layout()` to prevent overlapping elements
- `fig, ax = plt.subplots(constrained_layout=True)` is recommended for automatic spacing
- For large datasets, use `rasterized=True` in plot calls to reduce file size
This skill includes helper scripts in the `scripts/` directory:
- **`references/plot_types.md`** - Complete catalog of plot types with code examples and use cases
- **`references/styling_guide.md`** - Detailed styling options, colormaps, and customization
- **Jupyter** - Interactive plotting with `%matplotlib inline` or `%matplotlib widget`
3. **Memory issues with many figures**: Close figures explicitly with `plt.close(fig)`
4. **Font warnings**: Install fonts or suppress warnings with `plt.rcParams['font.sans-serif']`
- Avoid rainbow colormaps (jet) - they are not perceptually uniform
2. **State confusion**: Use OO interface to avoid pyplot state machine issues

content.value_statement: Python users need clear plots that are accurate, readable, and ready to share. This skill gives Matplotlib workflows, styling guidance, export settings, and troubleshooting support.
actual_capabilities: Explains line, scatter, bar, histogram, heatmap, contour, box, violin, and 3D plot workflows.
Guides object-oriented Figure and Axes usage for maintainable Matplotlib code.
Covers styling with colors, colormaps, rcParams, grids, legends, labels, and annotations.
Shows export choices for PNG, PDF, SVG, transparent backgrounds, DPI, and tight bounding boxes.
Includes a plot template script with common visualization examples.
Includes a style configurator script for generating Matplotlib style files.
limitations: It does not verify the statistical correctness of the source data.
Helper scripts require a local Python environment with Matplotlib and related packages installed.
Interactive plots depend on the active notebook, GUI, or backend configuration.
Final visual quality still depends on fonts, figure size, labels, and export settings.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Figures
use_cases.description: Create readable plots with labels, legends, color choices, and publication-ready export settings.

use_cases.title: Explore Business Data
use_cases.description: Build quick charts for trends, distributions, category comparisons, and correlation views.

use_cases.title: Teach Plotting Concepts
use_cases.description: Explain Matplotlib hierarchy, subplot layouts, styling choices, and common troubleshooting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Simple Plot
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Matplotlib line plot for my x and y values. Add a title, axis labels, grid, and legend.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: I have this dataset and goal. Recommend the best Matplotlib chart type and explain the design choices.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Publication Figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this Matplotlib figure for a paper. Focus on layout, labels, colors, DPI, file format, and accessibility.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Panel Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reusable Matplotlib workflow for a multi-panel scientific figure with shared axes, annotations, and export settings.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a chart comparing monthly revenue across three regions.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a grouped bar chart, names the required data columns, and describes labels, legend placement, and export settings.

output_examples.input: A researcher has a crowded figure with overlapping titles and labels.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests object-oriented axes control, constrained layout, smaller annotations, clearer labels, and a publication export checklist.

output_examples.input: A notebook user wants a heatmap of a correlation matrix.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a heatmap approach with a colorbar, diverging colormap, readable tick labels, and a saved figure option.

best_practices: Use the object-oriented Figure and Axes API for reusable and maintainable plots.
Choose colorblind-friendly colormaps and include labels that explain the data clearly.
Set figure size, layout, DPI, and output format before exporting final figures.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on pyplot global state for complex figures with multiple axes.
Do not use rainbow colormaps for ordered data because they can mislead readers.
Do not export final figures without checking label overlap, legend placement, and resolution.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Matplotlib charts, scientific plots, styled figures, subplots, and exported graphics.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create publication-ready figures?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers layout, labels, accessibility, DPI, vector formats, and transparent or white backgrounds.

faq.question: Does it include executable helper scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes local Python scripts for plot templates and style configuration.

faq.question: Will it choose the best chart for my data?
faq.answer: It can recommend chart types based on your goal, data shape, and comparison needs.

faq.question: Can it fix common Matplotlib errors?
faq.answer: It includes troubleshooting guidance for layout issues, state confusion, fonts, memory, and export settings.
